newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cotton group votes to seek Step 2 payments.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cotton group votes to seek Step 2 payments.

text.p: National Cotton Council's board of directors unanimously voted Wednesday to ask the government for so-called Step Two payments even if world prices are comparatively high.
"We've been discussing this for several months. It has been our top issue and was at this meeting," said a spokesman for the group. "We'll now begin to develop a strategy for moving this forward."

The industry group wants to eliminate a rule that bars Step Two payments whenever a special U.S. import quota, allowing more cotton to enter the country than normal, was in effect due to a 10-week run of high prices.

The group also will ask the government to allow Step Two payments until the Average World Price -- a calculation made by the Agriculture Department -- equals 134 percent of the loan rate. Currently, payments are made until the AWP exceeds 130 percent.

Under the 1996 farm policy law, so-called Step Two payments or certificates must be issued to users or exporters whenever the U.S.-Northern Europe price for upland cotton, calculated by USDA, is more than 1.25 cents higher than Northern Europe prices and the Average World Price does not exceed 130 percent of the loan rate.
The 1996 farm law limited Step Two expenditures to $701 million from fiscal 1996-2002.
